mcqs.question: According to the triangle law of vector addition, how is the resultant of two vectors A and B obtained?

options.A: Place the tail of B at the head of A and draw the vector from the tail of A to the head of B
options.B: Place the tail of A at the head of B and draw the vector from the tail of B to the head of A
options.C: Place the vectors tail‑to‑tail and draw the vector from the common tail to the midpoint of the line joining the heads
options.D: Place the vectors head‑to‑head and draw the vector connecting the tails

mcqs.answer: Place the tail of B at the head of A and draw the vector from the tail of A to the head of B
mcqs.explanation: The triangle law states that if you place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first, the resultant is the vector drawn from the free tail to the free head. Option A describes this correctly; the other options describe unrelated constructions.

mcqs.question: The parallelogram law of vector addition says that when two vectors are represented as adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the resultant vector is:

options.A: One of the sides of the parallelogram
options.B: The diagonal that starts from the common initial point of the two vectors
options.C: The diagonal that starts from the opposite corner of the common initial point
options.D: The sum of the magnitudes of the two vectors

mcqs.answer: The diagonal that starts from the opposite corner of the common initial point
mcqs.explanation: When two vectors are placed tail‑to‑tail, completing the parallelogram gives a diagonal from the opposite corner to the common tail; this diagonal represents the vector sum. Option C captures this, while the other options misstate the law.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the polygon law for adding multiple vectors?

options.A: It can be applied only when exactly two vectors are involved
options.B: It states that vectors can be placed head‑to‑tail to form a closed polygon, and the resultant is the vector joining the start and end points
options.C: It requires all vectors to be parallel to each other
options.D: It gives the magnitude of the resultant as the product of the individual magnitudes

mcqs.answer: It states that vectors can be placed head‑to‑tail to form a closed polygon, and the resultant is the vector joining the start and end points
mcqs.explanation: The polygon (or head‑to‑tail) method extends the triangle law: by arranging any number of vectors head‑to‑tail, the resultant is the vector from the first tail to the final head. Options A, C, and D are incorrect descriptions.

mcqs.question: A vector of magnitude 5 N acts eastward and another of magnitude 12 N acts northward. What is the magnitude and direction of the resultant vector?
mcqs.explanation: Resultant magnitude = √(5²+12²)=13 N. Direction = tan⁻¹(12/5)=67.4° measured north of east. Option A matches both values; the others are incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: Two vectors are drawn head‑to‑tail: one 8 cm long making 30° above the horizontal, and the other 6 cm long along the horizontal. Using a graphical addition, what is the approximate magnitude of the resultant?
mcqs.explanation: Resolving components: 8 cos30°≈6.93 cm (horizontal) and 8 sin30°=4 cm (vertical). Adding the horizontal 6 cm gives 12.93 cm horizontal, 4 cm vertical. Resultant ≈√(12.93²+4²)≈13.5 cm. Option B is correct; the others are off.

mcqs.question: Vector B has magnitude 15 N and is directed 60° north of east. Vector A has magnitude 10 N directed east. What is the magnitude of the vector obtained by subtracting A from B (i.e., B – A)?
mcqs.explanation: Components of B: 15 cos60°=7.5 N east, 15 sin60°≈13.0 N north. Subtract A (10 N east): east component = 7.5 – 10 = –2.5 N (west), north = 13.0 N. Magnitude = √((-2.5)²+13.0²)≈13.2 N. Option B is correct; others result from incorrect subtraction or ignoring direction.

mcqs.question: A student says that when a 5 N eastward vector and a 5 N northward vector are added using the triangle law, the resultant magnitude is 10 N because the magnitudes simply add. Which statement best identifies the flaw in this reasoning?

options.A: The triangle law can be used only for vectors that are parallel
options.B: Magnitudes add directly only when the vectors are collinear (along the same line)
options.C: The resultant magnitude is always equal to the larger of the two vectors
options.D: The direction of the resultant does not affect its magnitude

mcqs.answer: Magnitudes add directly only when the vectors are collinear (along the same line)
mcqs.explanation: Vector addition follows the triangle law geometrically; magnitudes add directly only for collinear vectors. Here the vectors are perpendicular, so the resultant magnitude is √(5²+5²)=7.07 N, not 10 N. Option B pinpoints the misconception; the other options are unrelated.

mcqs.question: Two vectors of equal magnitude 8 N act at an angle of 120° to each other. Using the parallelogram law, what is the magnitude of the resultant?
mcqs.explanation: Resultant magnitude = √(A²+B²+2AB cosθ) = √(64+64+2·64·cos120°) = √(128–64) = √64 = 8 N. Option B matches this calculation; the other options arise from incorrect use of the formula or ignoring the angle.
